'''''Coleus barbatus''''', also known by the synonyms '''''Plectranthus barbatus''''' and incorrectly '''''Coleus forskalaei''''' (and other spellings of this [[Binomial nomenclature#Codes|epithet]]), is a tropical perennial plant related to the typical [[coleus]] species. It is known by the common name '''woolly plectranthus'''. It produces [[forskolin]], an [[extract]] useful for [[pharmaceutical]] preparations and research in [[cell biology]].<ref name="planta">{{cite journal|pmid=20178070|year=2010|last1=Alasbahi|first1=R. H.|title=Plectranthus barbatus: A review of phytochemistry, ethnobotanical uses and pharmacology - Part 1|journal=Planta Medica|volume=76|issue=7|pages=653–61|last2=Melzig|first2=M. F.|doi=10.1055/s-0029-1240898|bibcode=2010PlMed..76..653A |doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Name==
[[File:Plectranthus barbatus (26409949835).jpg|thumb|upright=0.7|Flowers]]
The Brazilian name is {{lang|pt|boldo brasileiro}} ({{IPA|pt|ˈbowdu bɾaziˈlejɾu|pron}}), or {{lang|pt|boldo gaúcho}}, as opposed to the Chilean true [[boldo]]; {{lang|pt|boldo-da-terra}} ({{IPA|pt|ˈbowdu dɐ ˈtɛʁɐ|pron}}); {{lang|pt|boldo-de-jardim}} ({{IPA|pt|ˈbowdu dʒi ʒaʁˈdʒĩ|pron}}); or {{lang|pt|tapete-de-[[:pt:Oxalá|Oxalá]]}} ({{IPA|pt|tɐˈpetʃi dʒoʃaˈla|pron}}; 'Oxalá's carpet', because of its [[velvet]]y texture).

In the [[French Caribbean]], it is called "doliprane" (from the brand name of a [[paracetamol]]-based drug) because of its uses as a [[painkiller]] in [[folk medicine]].

==Description==
It is a semi-[[succulent]] plant that grows as a subshrub to 1.5 m high by 1.5 m wide. The oppositely arranged leaves are relatively large with serrated leaf edges. Purple-blue flowers grow on upright [[racemose]] inflorescences that are up to 25 centimeters long.<ref name= Kew>[https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:60454692-2#:~:text=The%20native%20range%20of%20this,the%20seasonally%20dry%20tropical%20biome. Coleus barbatus] by [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]]. Retrieved 3 November 2024.</ref>

==Taxonomy==
[[File:Plectranthus barbatus kz02.jpg|thumb|right|Leaf detail]]
''Coleus barbatus'' was first described by [[Henry Cranke Andrews]] in 1810 as ''Plectranthus barbatus''.<ref name=IPNI_454267-1/> It was transferred to ''Coleus'' by Bentham in 1830.<ref name=IPNI_60454692-2/><ref name=POWO_60454692-2/> Although ''Coleus'' was previously sunk into ''Plectranthus'', the original binomial was revived in a major study of the subtribe Plectranthinae in 2019.<ref name=PatoMwanGovaSmit19/>

There has been some confusion over the synonyms of this species. ''Plectranthus forskaolaei'' was first described by Vahl in 1790.<ref name=Vahl90>{{Citation |last1=Vahl |first1=M. |date=1790 |contribution=Plectranthus Forskålaei |title=Symbolae Botanicae |page=44 |oclc=475396338 |contribution-url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/38534783 |access-date=2020-07-31 |issue=1 }}</ref> Vahl's name is illegitimate, because he treats it as a synonym of the earlier described ''Ocimum hadiense'' <small>Forrsk.</small> Vahl spelt the epithet as "''Forskålaei''",<ref name=Vahl90/> referring to [[Peter Forsskål|Pehr Forsskål]], whose surname is also spelt "Forskål".<ref name=IPNI_a12502-1/> The [[International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants]] at Art. 60.7 specifies that "å" is to be replaced by "ao".<ref name=ShenzhenCode60/>

Willdenow in 1800 referred to Vahl's name, but spelled the epithet "''forskolaei''".<ref name=Will00/> ({{As of|2020|July|31}}, the ''[[International Plant Names Index]]'' had the spelling "''forskalei''".<ref name=IPNI_454397-1/>) It was probably this species that Briquet referred to when transferring a species to ''Coleus'' as "''C. forskohlii'' <small>(Willd.) Briq.</small>", introducing yet another spelling of the epithet; however, Briquet did not explicitly refer to a [[basionym]]. Briquet regarded "''Coleus forskohlii''" as synonymous with what he called  "''C. barbatus'' <small>Benth.</small>",<ref name=Briq97/> although Vahl had originally given a different synonymy. Paton et al. (2019) state that the epithets "''forskalaei''" or "''forskohlii''" are incorrectly applied to this species, instead treating binomials with these epithets as synonyms of ''[[Coleus hadiensis]]'', in accordance with Vahl's original use.<ref name=PatoMwanGovaSmit19/>

==Distribution==
The distribution area extends from [[tropical Africa]] across the [[Arabian Peninsula]] to parts of [[South Asia]] and [[East Asia]]. It is native to [[Burundi]], China South-Central, [[East Himalaya]], [[Eritrea]], [[Ethiopia]], [[India]], [[Kenya]], [[Nepal]], [[Oman]], [[Rwanda]], [[Saudi Arabia]], [[Somalia]], [[Sri Lanka]], [[Sudan]], [[Tanzania]], [[Thailand]], [[Uganda]], [[Yemen]] and [[Zaïre]].<ref name= Kew/>

==Chemistry==
[[File:Forskolin.svg|thumb|right|120px|Chemical structure of [[forskolin]]]]
[[Herbal tea]]s made from ''Coleus barbatus'' contain [[rosmarinic acid]] and also [[flavonoid]] [[glucuronide]]s and [[diterpenoid]]s.<ref name=Fale>{{cite journal | author = Falé, P.L., Borges, C., Madeira, P.J.A., Ascensão, L.| title = Rosmarinic acid, scutellarein 4′-methyl ether 7-O-glucuronide and (16S)-coleon E are the main compounds responsible for the antiacetylcholinesterase and antioxidant activity in herbal tea of Plectranthus barbatus ("falso boldo") | journal = Food Chem. | year = 2009 | volume   =114 | issue = 3 | pages = 798–805 | doi=10.1016/j.foodchem.2008.10.015|display-authors=etal}}</ref><ref name=Porfirio>{{cite journal |vauthors=Porfírio S, Falé PL, Madeira PJ, Florêncio MH, Ascensão L, Serralheiro ML | title = Antiacetylcholinesterase and antioxidant activities of Plectranthus barbatus tea, after in vitro gastrointestinal metabolism | journal = Food Chem. | year = 2010 | volume = 122 | pages = 179–187 | doi=10.1016/j.foodchem.2010.02.044}}</ref>

[[Forskolin]], which derives its name from the incorrect binomial name of this plant, ''Coleus forskohlii'', has been isolated from the roots.<ref name=planta/><ref>{{cite book|last2=Murray|first1=Joseph E. | last1=Pizzorno| first2 = Michael T.|title=Textbook of Natural Medicine|date=2012|publisher=Churchill Livingstone|location=Edinburgh|isbn=9781437723335|page=686|edition=4th}}</ref>
